Here’s the relevant excerpt from the methodology section:

“The ultrasonic assisted potassium hydroxide pretreatment (KOH_Upt) was applied in 1 L of bottles. Fig. 1 shows the experimental setup and ultrasonic conditions applied during pretreatment. Three concentrations of KOH, 2%, 4%, and 6% (w/w) were applied. pH was used to predict the optimum time required for pretreatment process [25]. A ratio of 1:0.02–0.06:6 (w/w) for WS:KOH:H_2O was used during pretreatment. A required weight of KOH was first added in each bottle containing a pre-calculated amount of distilled water. In order to avoid any exothermic heat effects, KOH solutions were left for a short time interval (3–5 min) to achieve equilibrium. Finally, WS was added to KOH solution and was thoroughly mixed to attain the uniform distribution of moisture content, before starting ultrasonic process. The pretreatment was carried out in an ultrasonic bath (KH5200DE, Nanjing Xiao Equipment Company, China). The reason to apply bath ultrasonication process was to effectively handle the bulk amount of biomass in single run for each KOH concentration. Therefore, 50 g TSL^−1 of WS was applied in triplicate during each pretreatment. The ultrasonic bath was operated at temperature of (22 ± 1) °C (ambient temperature) and at constant intensity of 20 kHz. The water level in the ultrasonication bath was maintained above the biomass in order to provide maximum ultrasonication effect throughout the bottles. During ultrasonication, the bath temperature gradually increased, however, it was further calibrated to set point value by controlling bath water temperature.”

The text describes the use of an ultrasonic bath, specifying a frequency of 20 kHz and a temperature of 22 ± 1°C. It details the process of adding KOH to the WS and initiating the ultrasonic treatment.
